topic: Dissertation Literature Review: The Synthesis Matrix

copy.instagram:
Staring at 40 PDFs and feeling like you’re drowning? We’ve all been there—the 3 AM 'why did I pick this topic' spiral is a rite of passage. Most students fall into the trap of writing a 'book report' style review, summarizing one author after another. That’s a one-way ticket to a 2:2.

To hit that First-Class mark, you need to stop summarizing and start synthesizing. Think of your literature review as a debate between experts, not a list of names. 

Swipe through for the blueprint:

Slide 2: The Trap—Organizing by author or year. It’s descriptive, not critical.
Slide 3: The Fix—Thematic coding. Group by debates, methodology, or specific variables. 
Slide 4: The Secret—Identify the 'gap'. Where do these studies disagree? That’s where your research shines.

Save this for when you’re knee-deep in reading, and check the link in bio if you need a hand mapping your synthesis out. You’ve got this.

copy.facebook:
Is your dissertation literature review feeling more like a never-ending laundry list of authors? I see so many students lose marks here because they get stuck in 'book report' mode—summarizing every paper chronologically instead of actually engaging with the research.

If you want that First-Class grade, shift your focus to a Synthesis Matrix. Here is how to pivot:

• Stop organizing by author: It makes your argument fragmented.
• Start coding by theme: Group studies by their theoretical findings or methodological limitations.
• Find the friction: Your marker wants to see where the authors disagree. That’s your 'knowledge gap'—the golden ticket for your own research.
• Compare methodologies: Don't just report results; critique how they got there.

It’s a heavy lift, but you don't have to do it alone. If you’re stuck on your structure or need help mapping out your themes, send me a message on WhatsApp at +91 95098 93638 and let's get you back on track. We'll get that draft sorted together.
